slice.hypothesis: An already-exposed non-GitHub Chat connector may expose a native concurrency-safe durable mutation that can remove one class of richer-mode state coordination dependency.
slice.tested_surface: set_event_label_silently plus comparison to generic update_event schema
slice.tested_scope: Current Chat-exposed tool contract only. No calendar, event, label, contact, attendee, or other user data was read or mutated.

evidence.set_event_label_silently_contract: The connector states that missing ETags fail before any write and concurrent updates are protected with the current ETag. The mutation is restricted to a primary-calendar event private label, sends no attendee updates, and preserves shared fields.
evidence.generic_update_event_contract: The generic update_event schema exposes event_id and mutable event fields but no caller-supplied ETag/version precondition or idempotency key.
evidence.reason_live_execution_omitted: This bounded leaf was capability discovery only and the role contract forbids consuming user semantic data merely to test connector capability.

slice.mechanism: A connector-internal read/current-ETag/write path can reject concurrent stale mutations for the exact private-label operation, providing a provider-specific lost-update guard without external hosted compute or a manual arbitration step.
slice.expected_upside: Potential narrow durable coordination cell for scheduled Chat if label value/readback semantics are sufficient; materially stronger than retrieval-only Files surfaces for lost-update protection.
slice.downside: The precondition token is internal rather than caller-supplied, the operation is specialized to an existing primary-calendar event label, arbitrary payload storage is unproven, and no generic idempotency key is exposed.
slice.smallest_cheap_test: On a later invocation, schema-audit only the Calendar label create/list/read and event-label readback contracts to decide whether the specialized ETag-protected label mutation can encode a deterministic finite-state CAS cell without reading or mutating user data.
failure_modes: No caller-visible version token means arbitrary compare-and-set semantics may be impossible even though the connector internally uses ETags.
An existing Calendar account, event, and named label may be required, so the mechanism is not provider-independent persistence.
A label field may have insufficient payload cardinality for general checkpoints or idempotency records.
Connector-contract presence does not prove runtime behavior on an unobserved account; no user-data test was performed.
Zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental cost are not established by the tool schema alone, so this slice cannot count as Phase-1 acceptance.

conflict_check: Used only current manifest/lifecycle/DESIRED/cross_field role controls, own cross_field LATEST, and the current Chat-exposed Google_Calendar tool schema. No O, downstream, other-worker, legacy, shared-ledger, receipt, or user semantic data was consumed.
frontier: Google Calendar exposes a specialized connector-internal current-ETag guard for silent private-label writes; generic caller-controlled CAS/idempotency remains unproven.
Determine whether Calendar label/readback schemas can turn that specialized guarded mutation into a deterministic finite-state coordination cell without live user-data access.
GitHub SHA-CAS remains the strongest previously verified provider-specific generic conditional-write primitive in own state; live stale-SHA/lost-response retry remains untested.
Provider-independent durable state remains unresolved; a provider-specific specialized write is not a parity acceptance result.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r245 from LATEST plus this exact checkpoint. Do not repeat the conversation-Files or generic Google Calendar update audits.
